timeline.description: Manufacturers across the consumer appliance sector are gearing up for price hikes, anticipating increases of 5% to 10% from October due to surging material and freight costs. Brands like Blue Star and Haier are adjusting their pricing strategies, especially with rising copper costs affecting multiple categories. Although existing stock may cushion the blow momentarily, new prices will kick in after Diwali, potentially impacting festive consumer sentiment.

timeline.title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG train, launches Rs 1,542 crore railway projects
timeline.description: Amit Shah inaugurated India's first LNG-powered train and several railway projects valued at over Rs 1,542 crore. The LNG-powered train utilizes a dual-fuel system, helping to significantly reduce diesel consumption. Shah also laid the foundation for the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system, targeting enhanced railway safety. Additionally, the Sabarmati-Sarkhej railway line doubling project aims to improve connectivity and facilitate industrial growth.

timeline.title: California teens build AI fall-risk system, win $100,000 scholarship
timeline.description: California teenagers Ruoqi Li and Jason Yang developed SafeStrides, an AI-powered fall-risk system combining smartphone camera tracking and wearable sensors. The system analyses walking patterns, provides instant risk assessments and offers mobility and home-safety guidance. Their engineering project earned them recognition as 2026 Davidson Fellows and a shared $100,000 scholarship.

timeline.title: Switzerland's neutrality test puts Nato ties, Russia sanctions at stake
timeline.description: In a significant referendum, Swiss voters are deliberating over potential changes to the nation's established neutrality rules concerning military partnerships. The proposed amendment seeks to restrict Switzerland's involvement in peacetime alliances and its capacity to enforce sanctions. These discussions have gained traction following the imposition of sanctions against Russia during the Ukraine crisis, raising concerns over the integrity of Switzerland's neutrality.

timeline.title: Ed Sheeran concerts canceled at Gillette Stadium amid nor’easter warnings
timeline.description: Ed Sheeran's highly anticipated concerts set for Gillette Stadium on September 25 and 26 have been canceled due to severe weather conditions brought on by a nor'easter. The decision, made after discussions with local officials, prioritizes fan safety. Fans who purchased tickets through Ticketmaster will automatically receive refunds for these canceled shows.

timeline.description: In Madrid, a massive protest unfolded as tens of thousands rallied for stronger tenant protections amidst escalating rents and evictions. The poignant eviction of an elderly woman has spotlighted Spain’s ongoing housing crisis, sparking demands for measures to prevent fraud and a moratorium on evictions without alternative housing. With a notable shortage in rental properties, the housing dilemma continues to intensify despite recent economic growth.

timeline.title: Asian Games: Sindhu, Hooda exits cap India's disappointing badminton campaign
timeline.description: At the Asian Games 2026, India's badminton team concluded with just one medal. Both PV Sindhu and Unnati Hooda exited in the women's singles quarterfinals after fierce competition. The women’s doubles team fell to a strong Malaysian pair, and mixed doubles suffered a narrow defeat. A demanding tournament schedule took its toll on performance, highlighting a stark decline from their previous edition's achievements.

timeline.title: Slained Hamas chief's ex-bodyguard stayed as 'Mr. X' in UK, planned attacks on Jews
timeline.description: A former bodyguard linked to Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh has been apprehended in London due to his alleged involvement in planning attacks. Despite having British citizenship, his connections to Hamas's military faction raise questions about how he gained entry. This arrest, a result of a multinational operation involving Israeli intelligence, has led to extradition efforts aimed at moving him to Germany for further investigation of the accused attack scheme.

These principles emphasize user focus, speed, and the importance of democracy on the web. The company has continuously innovated to enhance access to information globally, catering to diverse languages and needs. Google's commitment to ethical advertising practices and mobile technology remains steadfast, allowing users to benefit from its services.

timeline.title: Missouri house transformed into ‘African Queen’ listed for $1.2 million
timeline.description: A 1962 house in Springfield, Missouri, known as the African Queen, is on the market for $1.2 million. Bought by Michael and Lisa Willhoit in 2013, the 3,176-square-foot home features a 15-foot Zulu warrior sculpture, a 20,000-piece crocodile mosaic, reclaimed teak, unusual light fixtures and a glass floor overlooking spring-fed water. It is currently used as a short-term rental.

timeline.title: Long Island entrepreneur grows garage startup into award-winning security firm
timeline.description: Founded in 2020 by Jawad Khalfan, SecureTech Systems has successfully executed over 1,500 installations. The company has shifted its focus from residential services to larger commercial security projects, earning accolades including the 2026 Next-Gen Entrepreneur of the Year award. This remarkable growth is driven by impactful projects in sectors such as education, healthcare, and commerce. SecureTech's expansion as a key technology partner in New York continues to thrive.

timeline.title: 25-year-old Gen Z techie earning Rs 1.8 lakh says Bengaluru homes are unaffordable
timeline.description: A 25-year-old cybersecurity professional in Bengaluru faces challenges with high housing prices despite earning a good salary. He initially thought he could afford a decent home with a Rs 1.3 crore budget. After exploring properties, he realized that affordability in major cities is increasingly difficult for young professionals. His experience raises questions about home ownership dreams among millennials and Gen Z.

timeline.title: AI in healthcare: promise, risks and patient safety | Episode 53
timeline.description: AI is increasingly being used in healthcare, including drug and vaccine development, medical imaging and clinical decision-making. While these applications may support research and clinical care, they also raise concerns about patient safety, inaccurate or misleading information, data privacy and the potential misuse of AI in biological research. In Episode 53 of Health Wrap, Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to Dr. Abdul Ghafur, infectious diseases expert, Apollo Hospitals, Chennai, about the opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence in healthcare. They discuss how AI could accelerate medical research, support doctors in clinical care, and why its limitations and potential risks need careful attention.

timeline.description: In responding to the backlash against actor Mammootty following his recent National Award recognition, Harisree Yousuf stood firmly in defense of the beloved star. timeline.title: One point short in 2018, Ahvar Rizvi gets his Asian Games chance eight years later
timeline.description: One point short of India’s 2018 Asian Games selection, Trap shooter Ahvar Rizvi spent the next seven years rebuilding his career after Double Trap was removed from the international programme. The 2018 junior world champion struggled with the transition, briefly quit shooting and later competed with teammate Lakshya Sheoran’s gun. Now, Rizvi has made his first Asian Games team and is preparing to represent India in Trap at Nagoya.

timeline.title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs summoned by Australia Senate over AI agent breach
timeline.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have received written requests to appear at a public hearing in Canberra on Thursday, according to a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young, the Australian Greens lawmaker chairing the inquiry. timeline.title: Psychiatrist explains why parents should rethink sending kids away to college
timeline.description: Parents are key players in their children's transition to college, providing essential support through discussions about substances prior to departure. Evidence suggests that effective parental communication can significantly lower the likelihood of risky behaviors involving alcohol and drugs. By fostering an open relationship, parents empower their children to seek assistance when necessary, ensuring they step into college life ready to make informed decisions and navigate challenges with confidence.

timeline.title: AI mural inspired by Banksy sparks backlash in Bristol
timeline.description: A newly unveiled AI-generated mural at the Jolly Colliers pub in Bristol has ignited backlash from local artists. They criticized inaccuracies in the depiction of renowned landmarks and raised concerns over the mention of Banksy. While the pub owner stated that the mural is a temporary fixture due to wall conditions, the episode has underscored deeper worries about technology's influence on artistic integrity and fair compensation for creativity.

timeline.title: Taiwan says US understands defence needs as $14 billion arms package remains on hold
timeline.description: Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister, Chen Ming-chi, emphasized that the United States is well aware of Taiwan's defense needs. Currently, Taiwan is waiting for a decision on a $14 billion arms deal, which the US has temporarily stalled. President Trump referred to this deal as a significant bargaining tool after his talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Meanwhile, China is continually strengthening its military prowess, creating ongoing challenges for Taiwan.

timeline.description: Mohanlal, the renowned actor, has nurturing an organic vegetable garden at his Elamakkara home in Kochi for years. During the 2021 lockdown, he engaged fans by sharing videos of his gardening endeavors, showcasing that even small spaces can yield fresh produce with methods like grow bags. This variety includes vegetables used in everyday cooking, all while he juggles his thriving acting career with his passion for sustainable farming.

timeline.title: Vijay Kumar Sharma becomes government teacher at 59 after clearing TGT, PGT
timeline.description: At 59, Uttar Pradesh resident Vijay Kumar Sharma has achieved his long-held dream of becoming a government teacher after 27 years of attempts. Sharma, who cleared TGT written examinations six times and PGT exams four times but missed final selection, has been appointed as a Sanskrit TGT at Ailum Inter College in Shamli. His 28-year-old daughter Mamta also cleared the recruitment examination and is currently on the waiting list. Sharma is expected to serve until retirement at 62.

timeline.title: Why kids behave differently with each parent, according to psychology
timeline.description: Children often exhibit different behaviors with each parent, reflecting the unique bonds formed through daily encounters. Such variations do not signify favoritism but instead showcase patterns of emotional safety and attachment. Factors like daily routines or emotional necessities shape their interactions. These behaviors reveal the child's comfort level with each caregiver. By grasping these dynamics, parents can support their child's emotional growth without fostering rivalry.

timeline.title: ‘Ma, they punched me’: Student’s last call to family; how horror unfolded at homestay
timeline.description: Nimisha Thakuria, a 22-year-old Gauhati University student, made a frantic phone call stating she could not breathe. After her family lost contact, she was found critically injured at a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati. Her alleged companion, Ashiq Ali, has been detained, stating that she hanged herself. Local residents have protested for a thorough investigation, linking the incident to broader societal issues.

timeline.title: Mark Feehily sues surgeon over weight-loss op that caused stomach removal
timeline.description: Westlife star Mark Feehily is suing bariatric surgeon Nick Carter in a £200,000 claim over complications following weight-loss surgery. Feehily alleges the procedure led to recurring sepsis and eventually required his entire stomach to be removed. Carter denies negligence and argues that the leak was a recognised complication of the procedure.

timeline.title: Rumours of ghost & ‘missing girls’ spark night-long protest at university in Punjab
timeline.description: Students at a private university in Rajpura protested due to false rumours about missing female students. The unrest began after a prank led to ghost stories linked to a supposed suicide. Police confirmed that no students were missing and that the reports were unfounded. The crowd clashed with police and vandalized vehicles during the protest. Authorities are investigating the source of the rumours while assuring that academic activities remain unaffected.

timeline.title: How 1,500 Christmas trees transformed a lake in 3 years
timeline.description: In an innovative study in southeastern Finland, researchers submerged 1,500 spruce trees in Lake Saimaa to analyze their influence on aquatic biodiversity. After a three-year period, the findings revealed a marked increase in benthic organisms. This experiment showcases how discarded Christmas trees could be creatively repurposed to foster healthier underwater ecosystems, shedding light on sustainable waste management strategies.
